matches.note: Printed under the Scotland/Ireland running head on p.51. p73r4 is only a cross-reference ('See page 51').
Findlay prints it as 'KINSALE OLD HEAD'. It is not p68r29, which is the Kinsale Harbour light at Fort Charles.
Findlay's 'Dungarvan' entry describes a white tower on Ballinacourty Pt.
Findlay prints 'HOOK POINT'. Its tower with red and white belts is Hook Tower.
Findlay prints 'SALTEES LT.-VESSEL', moored 'off Coningbeg Rock'. It sits between Dungarvan/Hook and Barrels in the coast order.
One report prints 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship', which is a slip. The station is the lighthouse, and Findlay has no light-vessel at Tuskar.
The row also gives the harbour pier light as item 2. The station is item 1, the head light.
One report prints it as 'Kirk Bank'. Findlay prints 'KISH LIGHTVESSEL'.
Findlay prints 'HOWTH-BAILEY'. It is not p70r12, which is Howth Harbour.
This light-vessel 'supersedes S. Rock lt.-ho.' (1877). It is not p71r0, the Skulmartin light-vessel (1886).

Findlay 1887 lists only the new MEW ISLAND light (1884). The old Copeland light on Lighthouse Island was discontinued and has no entry. The 1881–1883 reports probably came from the old light, so its position and character will differ from Findlay's for those years.
Findlay prints both Maidens towers as one row ('Two fixed bright lights … 800 yds. apart').
This is the same row as Maidens North: Findlay prints the pair together.
The light is on Altacarry, the N.E. point of Rathlin. Its upper and lower lights share one row.
Findlay prints 'INNISTRAHULL'.
Findlay prints 'FANNET POINT'. This is the Lough Swilly entrance light.

The reports print 'Killybegs', but Findlay's row called 'Killybegs' (p72r2) is the St. John Point (Donegal) light. Following your id, I matched the Rotten Island row. If the station was really St. John Point, use p72r2 instead.
One row covers both lights ('Two fixed bright lights; in one'). Findlay prints no longitude for it. It is not p72r5, the Black Rock at Sligo, a different light from the Mayo Blackrock.
The light is on Gubacashel Pt.
Findlay prints both Eagle Island towers as one row.
This is the same row as Eagle Island East.
At 54°4.2'N, 10°19.3'W this is the offshore Mayo rock, after Eagle Island in the coast order. It is not p72r5, the Sligo Black Rock.
Findlay prints 'Black Sod Quay'. The light is shown from a house on Black Sod Point.
Findlay prints both towers as one row. The N. light is the revolving one.
This is the same row as Slyne Head North. The S. light is the fixed one.
Findlay prints 'EERAGH ISLAND'. The reports' 'Arran Island N.' is this light.
One report prints 'Straw Island, S.', which is a slip for Arran Island S.
Findlay prints 'Tralee'. The light is 'On Little Samphire Island'.
Findlay prints 'TEARAGHT ISLAND'.
The tower was destroyed in the gale of 26 Nov 1881. That fits this station appearing only in 1881.

Findlay has no separate Dursey row. The Calf Rock row says a temporary light 'of same character is shown from lt.-ho. on S.W. extr. o[f Dursey Island]'. That matches Dursey taking over from Calf Rock in the 1882–1887 lists. Its position is not Calf Rock's: take it from the full description, which is cut off in the table.

notes:
Things to check:
(1) Rotten Island vs St. John Point (Donegal). The reports print 'Killybegs', and Findlay's row by that name (p72r2) is St. John Point. I followed your id and matched Rotten Island (p72r3); check which light the observer actually kept.
(2) Copeland. The only Findlay 1887 entry is the new Mew Island light (1884), so its character and position don't fit the old Copeland light for the 1881–83 reports.
(3) Dursey Island. It is only covered by the temporary-light note in the Calf Rock row, and that description is cut off. Read the full text on the p.56 scan to get the temporary light's position.
(4) Row ids skip several numbers: p69r9, p70r4, p71r10, p71r24, p72r4, p72r12, p72r16, p72r21. Check whether entries were dropped in transcription. None of these gaps is needed for a match, but p71r24 (between Innistrahull and Dunree) and p72r16 (just after Slyne Head) sit near matched stations.
(5) Transcription errors in the Findlay table, not affecting matches: Inishowen (p71r11) has lat 53 13.6, surely 55 13.6. Oyster Island (p72r6) and Inishgort (p72r14) are each missing a coordinate. Slyne Head's year column reads '1836 / null'.
(6) Printing slips in the reports' names: 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship' (it is the lighthouse), 'Kirk Bank' (Kish), and 'Straw Island, S.' (Inisheer).
(7) Every station has a Findlay 1887 entry, so none is null.
